# Draft:Edward Salazar Celis

----
Edward Salazar Celis is a Colombian writer and scholar specializing in Latin American and Latinx arts, fashion and visual cultures. He is the author of the books Nostalgias y aspiraciones: Vestir, estéticas y tránsitos de las clases medias bogotanas en la segunda mitad del siglo XX. and Estudios de la moda en Colombia the first fashion reader in the country. He is one of the most prominent authors on critical fashion studies in Latin America and is often cited in the academia and popular media. He was also the first TV host for Bogota Fashion Week in 2022
In Colombia, his essays have been published in El Malpensante, Cartel Urbano, Cero Setenta, among other cultural media. His work on Latinx fashion and aesthetics in the United States has been featured in [https://www.latinxproject.nyu.edu/intervenxions/the-absence-of-latinx-designers-in-fashion-archives The Latinx Project] and [https://revista.drclas.harvard.edu/black-is-a-working-class-color-the-latinx-politics-of-wearing-black/ Harvard Review of Latin America] as well as in academic sources such as Fashion Theory and the International Journal of Fashion Studies. His contribution aims to expand the study of fashioning Latinidades in academia and beyond, receiving award from the Mellon Foundation among others.
